主要内容: The video game industry is experiencing significant growth, with continued revenue and expanding engagement. According to Newzoo's Global Games Market Report, gamers worldwide are expected to spend around $138 billion on games this year, representing a 13.3 percent increase year over year. Samantha Greenberg, chief investment officer at Margate Capital Management, highlighted that the industry is transitioning from a hit-driven business to a recurring revenue model, with increased monetization opportunities beyond initial game purchases. Greenberg also emphasized the growing appeal of video games among young people, women, and college students, noting that more than half of teenagers play video games for several hours each day. She predicted the gaming trend will accelerate, with esports events like PGI 2018 gaining popularity. Take-Two Interactive, a video game holding company, was named as Greenberg's best stock idea, with a price target of $176. Electronic Arts was also highlighted by analyst Timothy O’Shea, with a $155 price target set on its shares. The video game industry is experiencing significant growth, outpacing the movie and television sectors. Epic Games, a privately held company, has reported over $1 billion in in-game revenue from its Fortnite Battle Royale game, according to data from SuperData. The game is free to download and play, and its success highlights the mainstream appeal of video games. O'Shea noted that the industry is becoming increasingly mainstream, while Greenberg emphasized that Fortnite taps into the interests of tweens and teens with its cartoonish design and pop culture elements. The game is also training users on in-game monetization and continuous purchases, even after the initial download.
